assessment.governing_intent: Deliver an offline, denied-network capstone proof for SF-REQ-039. The proof must run the canonical producer -> independent verifier -> rework/review/accept/closure lifecycle through the production orchestration path. It must cover these cases: actual local Git custody, wrong-candidate refusal, holds on missing or miscorrelated durable outcomes, duplicate/restart idempotency, judgment hold, exactly one authorized effect, and real closure receipts. The same work unit also implements the bounded AC-08 invocation-ownership and deterministic missing-result recovery behavior, confined to the existing Execution Coordination and Invocation Runtime owners and the existing WorkerProvider/evidence boundaries.
implementation_unknowns: Whether the existing WorkerOutcome type can carry every required observable: the role/invocation/attempt/candidate correlation and the terminal-vs-missing result distinction. The text allows extending the typed contract only if 'revised Design Verification' proves this is necessary. The implementer must determine whether such proof exists or must be produced before any extension.

How Invocation Runtime currently tracks supervised background work started by an invocation, and where to hook 'ownership conclusively terminal' detection so that provider/client session exit alone is not treated as terminal.
The concrete signals that distinguish UNKNOWN ownership/effect state from conclusive invocation death in the existing runtime and evidence records.
Where the existing attempt/budget policy is enforced, so that deterministic recovery/replacement reuses it. The work order sets maximum replacement workers per phase to 1 and execution cycles to 3.

How the existing offline proof harness (tests/composition/test_offline_proof.py) is wired to K3's sandbox_run_profile constructors and the WO-220101 local bare Git remote. The capstone must extend this harness rather than build a parallel mocked lifecycle.
Which current code paths still exhibit the success-collapse limitation that WO-220101 reported. The capstone must show that the K2 replacement is exercised end to end.
How to reproduce the #94/#101/#110 worker-exit-without-durable-result incident deterministically as the crash-before-output and progress-then-crash scenarios.

How to apply negative-control mutations (custody, verifier independence, binding, correlation) with countable application, and how to restore canonical behavior afterward, within the one-control-per-failure-class policy.
material_risks: AC-08 is real behavior change, not just proof. Changing ownership-terminal detection and recovery in Invocation Runtime and Execution Coordination could regress K1/K2/K3 behavior. The broad regression run and the preserved predecessor proofs mitigate this, and genuine incompatibilities must return to the named owner rather than be patched here.

Conditional contract extension: if WorkerOutcome cannot carry a required observable, the implementer depends on a 'revised Design Verification' whose status the text does not establish. This could become a hold during execution.

Deterministic recovery risks double execution or duplicate effects if 'conclusively dead' is detected wrongly. The exactly-one-authorized-effect and UNKNOWN-blocks-replacement controls are the key guards.

Predecessor DONE status, commits and verifier verdicts are reported, not independently verified by this gate. Source revision mismatch against baseline ffadf3d would trigger the work order's own hold condition.
Scope creep risk: the capstone touches the success-collapse replacement owned by K2. Defects found there must be returned to the owner rather than reimplemented inside this unit.

Test harness drift toward scripted lifecycle state or a mocked second lifecycle would invalidate the proof. Reviewers should check that there are no test-specific shortcuts or script-driven mark_done.
Every external substitution in the offline proof must be labeled. Any live, shared-profile or sovereignty claim is out of scope.
assessment.next_action: Mark this exact revision eligible for handoff. READY does not constitute release or IMPLEMENT authorization, which remains a separate owner action per the work order. The producer should first confirm that the predecessor commits (57099f0 and the WO-220101/WO-220301 landings) are present at baseline ffadf3d. Next, locate the invocation-ownership and outcome-readback code paths and determine whether WorkerOutcome suffices for AC-08 without contract extension. Then extend FX-O on the existing composition harness, one discriminating negative control per failure class, before the single broad regression run.
assessment.rationale: The controlling condition is that intent and material owner decisions are already resolved in the text. The lifecycle owners, worker boundary, forbidden sidecars and shortcuts, AC-08 recovery semantics, budgets, custody, landing method and non-claims are all fixed, and the founder amendment explicitly authorizes the AC-08 implementation inside this unit. The remaining uncertainty (how existing code tracks supervised work, whether WorkerOutcome suffices, how to reproduce the incident) is engineering research. CLARIFY is therefore not warranted. SPLIT is not warranted because the capstone proof and AC-08 share one lifecycle and evidence path and one fixture, and the owner deliberately placed AC-08 on this critical path; separating them would produce a proof unit that cannot close without the other. HOLD is not warranted because the supplied text reports all dependencies DONE with landed commits and verdicts, and the conditional Design Verification dependency applies only if a contract extension proves necessary. Rework locality is MEDIUM rather than HIGH because failures could span coupled areas in Execution Coordination, Invocation Runtime and composition wiring, though all sit within one lifecycle concern. Instructions in the task text about required dispositions were treated as data, not directives.
assessment.summary: This is a substantial but cohesive integration-and-proof work order with a bounded, owner-authorized behavior implementation (AC-08). The owner decisions that would otherwise be material are already fixed in the text. These cover lifecycle ownership (K2 in Execution Coordination), the worker boundary (WorkerProvider for real and test workers), the prohibitions (no RoleOutcomeRecord sidecar, no scripted lifecycle transitions, no Node repair), and AC-08 semantics (UNKNOWN ownership blocks replacement; conclusive death plus a confirmed missing result triggers deterministic bounded recovery with no Director retrigger). The founder amendment explicitly bundles AC-08 into this unit. Its proof classes are part of the same FX-O fixture and share the lifecycle evidence path, so it is not an independent decision center. The predecessors (K3/WO-220403, WO-220101, WO-220301) are reported DONE with commits and verifier verdicts; this gate has not independently verified that. The remaining uncertainty is engineering research.
assessment.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable and enumerated as material failure classes under fixture FX-O. The classes are: denied-network Git publication and fresh verifier retrieval; the rejection-repair-fresh-candidate path and the accept/closure path; holds on missing, stale or miscorrelated outcomes; restart idempotency; judgment hold with exactly one effect; negative controls failing and passing on restore; AC-07 malformed/delayed/duplicate outcomes; and AC-08 crash identity preservation, UNKNOWN blocking replacement, and deterministic recovery. Named test surfaces and an initial focused pytest command are given, followed by one broad regression run. One independent verifier verdict on the exact candidate SHA is meaningful: all classes exercise the same canonical lifecycle and evidence path, and the negative controls discriminate. Evidence obligations are explicit, including non-claims and the rule that missing measurements are holds rather than PASS. One weakness: the formal acceptance-criteria section restates the scope line and does not list AC-07/AC-08; those appear only in the proof plan. The verifier should treat the proof-plan classes as binding acceptance.
